results.note: All absolute counts are reference-policy-dependent: a support set is the set of decisions one frozen candidate is driven through. Only the patterns are claimed (set equalities, the budget at which certification flips, and the maximum min-blunder distance). The reversed-tie-break row demonstrates the dependence directly.

conjecture.status: unconditional form REFUTED at (4,4); survives only for SCALE-MATCHED grader/reference pairs. equality clause WITHDRAWN
conjecture.statement: When the grader's scale matches the scale the reference policy optimizes, the opponent tremble budget is at most the number of value classes below the root value AS THE OPPONENT SEES IT -- the blundering side is the one with rungs left to fall through. Mismatch the two and the bound does not merely loosen, it FAILS: a candidate indifferent to rungs the grader is scoring hands value back, and the opponent re-descends a ladder it had already fallen down.
refutations: (4,4) seat 0, class grading against the WDL-optimal V1 reference: budget 3 from drawn roots where the bound is 2; budget 2 from roots where the bound is 1; and -- decisively -- budget 2 from roots the opponent has ALREADY LOST outright, where the bound is 0 and no further fall should be possible at all.

The equality clause of the earlier form ('equality when the descent visits every intermediate class') fails in the other direction: at (3,3) seat 1 the class bound permits 3 at the 882 roots where the opponent is winning on attrition, and the observed budget is 1.
what_survives: Scale-matched pairs are unviolated everywhere tested: WDL grading against V1, and class grading against the class-optimal V2, at both sizes and both seats -- exhaustively at (3,3) (all 10,882 and 15,228 candidate-to-move roots). The (4,4) evidence is weaker than the word 'tested' suggests: the scan takes the 150 SHALLOWEST roots per value class within 8 ply, so the clean result there rests on a depth-biased subsample of 600 roots. A violation found in such a sample still refutes; a clean one does not confirm.

The failures are exactly the mismatched pair, and they are the same mechanism as the (4,4) seat-0 certification cliff: V1's indifference between losing outright and losing on the tiebreaker. Section C showed that mismatch manufactures gating states; this shows it also breaks the budget bound.
The mismatched pair is clean at (3,3) and refuted from (4,4) up -- the same size-dependence as Finding 8, and the same warning against reading a rule off the smallest board.
conjecture.why_not_a_law: What is left is an unproved upper bound with a scope condition found by testing it, exhaustive at one board size and sampled at one more. It is also loose where it would be informative: it forbids budgets nobody has observed rather than predicting the ones we do.
